data.title: Benzathine penicillin G
data.summary: III Antibiotics · Long-acting depot form of penicillin G (natural β-lactam)
data.body:
_Injectables · III Antibiotics_

**Class:** Long-acting depot form of penicillin G (natural β-lactam)

## Mechanism of action
- Binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits transpeptidation of the bacterial cell wall → bactericidal (needs actively dividing bacteria)
- Treponema pallidum divides slowly (every 30–33 h), so long, steady penicillin levels are needed — the benzathine salt gives low levels for 2–4 weeks

## Pharmacokinetics
- IM depot slowly releases penicillin G over 3–4 weeks
- Does not reach treponemicidal levels in CSF — not suitable for neurosyphilis
- Excreted by the kidneys

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Syphilis: primary, secondary, early latent (first choice); late latent and tertiary (non-neuro)
- Syphilis in pregnancy (the only adequate treatment; desensitise if allergic)
- Contacts of early syphilis; NACO white kit (kit 3, genital ulcer disease)
- Rheumatic fever prophylaxis; streptococcal pharyngitis; yaws, pinta, bejel

## Dose & formulations
- Early syphilis: 2.4 million units (MU) deep IM single dose (1.2 MU into each buttock)
- Late latent/unknown duration, tertiary (non-neuro): 2.4 MU IM once weekly × 3 weeks
- Congenital syphilis (asymptomatic infant, selected cases): 50,000 U/kg IM single dose
- Rheumatic fever prophylaxis: 1.2 MU every 3–4 weeks
- Reconstitute as per vial, inject deep IM with a wide-bore needle; observe for 30 min

## Adverse effects
- Jarisch–Herxheimer reaction (fever, chills, myalgia, worsening rash) within 2–24 h — from release of treponemal lipoproteins; commonest in secondary syphilis; manage with antipyretics; in pregnancy may cause preterm labour
- Anaphylaxis (rare; have adrenaline ready); urticaria, serum sickness
- Injection-site pain; accidental intravascular injection → Hoigné syndrome (with procaine penicillin) or Nicolau syndrome (embolia cutis medicamentosa — painful livedoid necrosis)

## Contraindications
- Penicillin allergy (in pregnancy or neurosyphilis → desensitise, do not substitute)
- Not for IV use; not for neurosyphilis

## Drug interactions
- Probenecid raises penicillin levels
- Tetracyclines (bacteriostatic) may antagonise

## Monitoring
- Non-treponemal titre (VDRL/RPR) at 3, 6, 12 (and 24) months; a four-fold fall (two dilutions) by 6–12 months shows adequate response
- Test for HIV and other STIs; trace and treat partners

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe and essential in pregnancy (old FDA category B). Compatible with breastfeeding.

## Viva points
- Drug of choice for all stages of syphilis except neurosyphilis (needs aqueous crystalline penicillin G IV)
- Jarisch–Herxheimer reaction vs drug allergy
- Nicolau syndrome — inadvertent intra-arterial injection
- Pregnant women with penicillin allergy must be desensitised
- Skin sensitivity testing is still commonly done in India before injection (keep adrenaline ready)

## Note on sources
Skin testing before benzathine penicillin is routine in many Indian hospitals; international guidelines (WHO/CDC) do not require it but stress readiness for anaphylaxis.

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.9; Khopkar ch.1; NACO STI guidelines. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
